parsed.why: No criminalisation of gender expression, no documented visitor-facing border or facility rules. Exposure is mainly resident-facing: no gender-marker route, workplace harassment, police failure at assemblies. Courts have struck down some expression limits.

New penal code criminalises same-sex conduct by birth-assigned sex, and reports show surging arbitrary arrests and abuse based on appearance or gender expression. No anti-discrimination recourse, and the junta's enforcement is state-driven.

Criminal statutes carry life imprisonment. Documented police custody torture, a 2024 abduction and beating of a trans activist, state-directed website blocking, and past witch hunts. Recent state-directed targeting is documented, with weak recourse.

Consensual same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2016, so no visitor criminal exposure. No explicit trans recognition or protection, and no documented trans-specific violence or border or facility data. Thin record with structural gaps; the only protection is in immigration detention.

De facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition, enforced through morality offences. Armed groups documented executing men accused of homosexuality for effeminate dress. No legal gender recognition and no LGBTI organisations, so recourse is absent.
